title: Strength restoration R1 for shoulder and ribcage health
summary: NH presents 'R1', a non-taxing superset of dumbbell pullovers and band/Spree face pulls that he does between sets on bench and upper-body days. Pullovers stretch the lats and rehab his intercostals after rib fractures; face pulls balance pressing and promote shoulder health and posture.

claims.claim: Insert a non-taxing 'strength restoration' superset between main sets on days that risk overuse injuries, to balance out the stress of the main lifts.
Heavy chest and front-delt work on bench/upper days pulls posture forward; the R1 superset (pullovers + face pulls) is meant to counterbalance it.
Pullovers can be done with cables, bands, dumbbells or an EZ bar; NH prefers dumbbells.
In the restoration superset, pullovers serve to stretch the lats and rehab the intercostal muscles of the ribcage.
NH broke both sides of his ribcage about 1.5-2 years earlier and still has chronic intercostal pain he must manage or risk re-breaking it.
Face pulls balance heavy pressing by training the rear delts and traps, giving a shoulders-back, straight-spine posture.
Restoration pullovers should use a weight you can do 12-15 times with no problem; it should not be taxing.
The more you extend your arms on pullovers, the more the triceps long head is involved, so account for prior long-head work.
Do restoration face pulls for 8-12 reps between main sets, finishing in a double-biceps position with shoulder external rotation.
With a band, leaning back makes face pulls easier and pulling further back makes them harder; long-term band use stops being felt, so he prefers a Spree device.
Face pulls with rotating handles (Spree) are easier on the wrists, useful for people with wrist issues.

exercises.name: Dumbbell pullover
cues: push with the legs to increase the stretch
more arm extension = more triceps long head
